12012.d:
Vanilla javascript and some css on SVG from bitmap input.

Press "p" to download a 2000x2000 pixels png image (if"opened" in full page)
Press "s" to download a SVG image (if"opened" in full page)
Press "l" to load and use an image of yours (if"opened" in full page)

The most interesting aspect of this work is the use of some public domain artwork bitmap images as input dataset to generate a randomized grid of blended triangular surfaces.

Triangle is the basic shape from wich it's possible to construct all other shapes, at least on a finite discrete grid like our screens. How not to adore triangles blessing our screen?

The goal of this work is not trying to catch the "essential", the "vibe", or the "atmosphere" from an input artwork, neither to parasite it and shine with it's reflected light. The input images are a way to random noise, but you can use your own and  you'll see that Triagulatria's own caracter will be preserved and you'll have even more good time.


Note1: I tuned and selected different configurations of Triangulatria. Some of them in some cases may produce just a black square. It's a valid artistic outcome but I will reserve some mints to exchange them with the black ones, at my sole discretion (ask me for the change if you want it)

Note2: On some browsers (for example Firefox) some configuration in some cases may request a lot of computational effort for "painting" the SVG and the device may get stuck for long time. As the result is likely to happen, I decided to keep those configurations, waiting for technology to cope with actual limits. Sorry for the bad user experience.

In an undiscovered area, you've stumbled upon an unknown creature.
It looks weirdly haunting, and you're feeling a sense of unease.

Is it communicating?

(to whom?)

Setting aside your discomfort for a moment, you're realizing you could be seeing it wrong.
While the creature does look eerie and its motivations are unclear,
you realize every culture has its own appreciation of aesthetics,
and you can't help noticing there is a certain grace to this performance.

And it all makes sense.

You're witnessing uncharted explorations of elegance.

The piece evokes a sense of digital entanglement. Sometimes it feels as though  we our  trapped and controlled by various algorithms. Social media companies are incentivized by profit  to manipulate our emotions and keep us on the app for as long as possible. The apps show us funny, sad, raunchy  and scary  content selected  to keep people scrolling and clicking endlessly entangled in the algorithm.  The machine toying with my human emotions.

12106.d:
Giorgio de Chirico was a prominent influence on the Surrealist movement. De Chirico’s art portrays dream-like and distorted worlds that encourage viewers to explore their subconscious. 

I am fascinated by the different ways artists have found to express esoteric concepts. In particular, I am interested in how artists like Giorgio de Chirico have used light and color to create ethereal images. 

I believe that the Abstract Temples project is a perfect example of how generative art can be used to create metaphysical artwork. By invoking the visual language of the dream world, these images invite you to explore the nebulous relationship between external and internal space.

In addition to the influence of Giorgio de Chirico, I would also like to credit James Turrell as an inspiration for this project. Turrell is an artist who creates installations that play with our perception of light and space. Turrell’s work has profoundly impacted my understanding of how art can create an immersive and disorienting experience. 

Each temple room is randomly generated from a selection of 16 templates. The templates include a variety of randomized features, including the color palette, celestial objects, design variations, and other effects. They also contain a rare secret. 

This project was created with p5js. 

Features:
-16 room templates
-18 color palettes
-Celestial objects
-Secrets

12137.d:
This work alludes to the need for rethinking our dependencies on primary sense faculties. In recent times we have seen with the explosion of web3, we are blinded by beautiful visuals so much that we are not able to see anything else anymore. Can beauty be described, or felt, or touched, can it touch us in that process? These were some of the questions that resulted in giving direction to this work, where the challenge was to create a simple landscape using descriptive labels, so that the landscape might be seen in a different light.

Also over the years having worked with differently abled people, the motivation also was to create a work that is inclusive and the beauty of a visual that can be enjoyed by everyone. With this in mind, I tried to create this work that uses the p5.js accessibility library, so that a description of the visual can be read by a screen reader.

Pressing '1' generates a text output of the visual the can be read by the screen reader, and 's' saves the current image. 

I had a few challenges in using the accessibility package, and had to resort to a basic version of the work to make the library usable for me, and much needs to be done in terms of it being user friendly for the general public. To that effect, 50% of the sales from the work will be donated to The Processing Foundation, to help with developing the accessibility library further. Also 66.66 % of the royalties will be perpetually split between The Processing Foundation and the first minter.

The weekday series is an ongoing exercise in the art of letter drawing through use of digital tools. Letters are designed within a 3D program and rendered out for additional compositing. Using the days of the week as an anchor, each letter study gives an opportunity to explore the relationship between depth and motion and the meanings we make of communication and design where these elements interact.

This week’s letter study was focused on creating uniform designs. The best way I could think to do this was with a generative design made with Cables. This patch uses a mixture of both text meshes and texture effects ops to iterate through incoming arrays of text data and manipulates that data to create 7 unique posters for each day of the week. 

The design features 105 possible combinations:
15 colorway options +
7 days of the week

Color palette

12164.d:
Some cities trace their depression in a line (^^^^...__....---)
Succession of points that affect the subject by their route.

El Bajo is a mashup city where many conflicts coexist, typical of being next to a metropolis city. El Bajo is like a port without a river, where there are abandoned railway stations, many street vendors, fairs, immigrants, it is the entrance and exit of the city where the flow of people is massive.

Its steep slope is due to the fact that in the seventeenth century it was close to a river that no longer exists today.

El Bajo defines an aesthetic by itself, bordering on kitsch, collage, perhaps typical of a Latin city, a city that seems stopped in time, a cultural mashup.

The levels of weirdness in the project are given by those factors that seem to be invisibilized that are mimetized with the city, the car window cleaners, some old trees, food carts, abandoned architecture that today is covered with bushes and humidity, textures and colors, the vibrations are continuously with the city.

We all have a story to tell about El Bajo, now it's your turn walking through the city of El Bajo.

12227.d:
The existing nature grows on the unexisting spirits.

Generative sketch, based on the pen and ink drawings of Po Sheng Chen. Po Sheng Chen is an Architect who has drawn nothing but Architecture for over 25 years. He tried to explore something different from his previous style (Brutalism with Magical Realism), so developed his own Minimalist Architecture process and style. After breaking up all the complicated elements and symbols, he chose a simple and naive way to present “pure volumes in the space (the essential of Architecture)”: the Use of different densities of vertical lines to create different faces of volumes, with the addition of horizontal lines to create shadows on the volumes. Shadow determined the form of volumes, then they became a clear composition in the space, Eliminating chaos. These lines seem like spirits to Po Sheng Chen, because they represent the soul of Architecture, but they do not have a specific form or meaning...they are between existing and unexisting! Tezumie is a creative generative artist. He saw the latest experimental drawings of Po Sheng Chen, and after reaching out, the collab was formed with the goal of creating a digital representation of the original concept surrounded by a natural and overgrown environment. The combination of nature and architecture.

Made in p5js.

12238.d:
Curved Truchet tiling is laid down on a 3D plane forming an imaginary landscape of ripples.

The longest continuous line created by the tiling is removed, cutting a path through the terrain.
This occurs within 3D space and may or may not appear within the confines of the canvas frame,
but most likely will appear.

A tower rises up to wherever a circle is created by the tiling. Driven by the random
tiling, zero or several of these may appear within the frame. Shadows differ in each mint.

In addition to working on decorative tiling, Sébastien Truchet worked on canals and sundials,
forming the inspiration for the exploration of shade and shadow in this work.

Mints will have a variety of earth-tone background colors with each perspective of the scene
slightly different to produce diverse results.

As I researched Sébastien Truchet I learned that he worked with hydraulics and canal design,
as well as sundials. This became the inspiration for my new shading and shadowing technique used
in this piece.

For me this piece evokes a sense of agriculture, and connects me to an imaginary
landscape that could have looked familiar to Truchet in 18th century France.

This work was created with my own javascript, utilizing my polyline path helper library I
maintain at https://github.com/markroland/path-helper.

12245.d:
• Tales of icebergs. •


I will tell you the most beautiful story
that stayed in my memory. Once upon a time, In the icy oceans.. the waters were calm, and the sky was stormy, but silent, silent as a Sunday afternoon in winter.

There he was.. they? that? I can't say for sure what, I know what I saw, I saw icebergs gathered, how a city had wires, poles, light, and that, that... 
A huge idol in the middle, shimmered like polished silver, shimmered as if the sky was clear and the sun hit directly. I'll never forget that. It was beautiful."

-

The iceberg cuts its facets from within.
Like jewelry from a grave
it saves itself perpetually and adorns
only itself, perhaps the snows
which so surprise us lying on the sea.
Good-bye, we say, good-bye, the ship steers off
where waves give in to one another's waves
and clouds run in a warmer sky.
Icebergs behoove the soul
(both being self-made from elements least visible)
to see them so: fleshed, fair, erected indivisible.



by Gen Doodler | twitter.com/GenDoodler
